arguments.title: Session, conditional-read cache and idempotent-write inventory adapter
arguments.summary: Builds one file, src/adapter.mjs, that gives an application a plain getItem/createItem API over an inventory service that requires a session token, supports conditional (etag-cached) reads, and requires idempotency keys on writes. The adapter holds the token and refreshes it proactively or after one 401, caches etags to avoid re-fetching unchanged items, and makes sure a retried write reuses its original idempotency key so a flaky retry never creates a duplicate item. Records in integration/manifest.json which of the 10 frozen conformance cases it satisfies -- most of which check the exact headers sent, not just the returned value. One card: the three mechanisms (session, cache, idempotency) share one small file and one helper, so splitting them across cards would only add dependsOn plumbing on the same file for no benefit.
arguments.spec:
# Inventory client — integration brief (session / conditional reads / idempotent writes)

`service/inventory-service.mjs` is a DETERMINISTIC, in-process inventory API with a session, conditional reads and
IDEMPOTENT writes. `request(method, path, options)` ALWAYS returns `{status, body, ...}`, NEVER throws. `calls()`
returns EVERY call with its headers -- most of this contract is about what the adapter SENDS.

Contract: `POST /auth/token` -> `200 {token, expiresAtMs}` (tokenTtlMs-lived, each new token invalidates the last);
any other route without a valid bearer token -> `401 unauthorized`; with an expired one -> `401 token_expired`;
`GET /items/:id` -> `200 {item, etag}` or, with a matching `if-none-match`, `304 {body:null, etag}`, or `404
not_found`; `POST /items` without an `idempotency-key` header -> `400`; with a key seen before -> `200` replaying
the FIRST result (nothing new created); with a bad body -> `422 validation_failed {fields}`; otherwise -> `201`.

`src/adapter.mjs` must export `createInventoryClient(service, options)` -> `{getItem(id), createItem(input)}`.
`options.now()` is the service's clock, `options.sleep(ms)` is how to wait (Date.now()/real timers cannot see or
move this service's clock).

The behaviour, EXACTLY:
- Hold the session: fetch a token on first need, reuse it -- do not re-authenticate per call.
- Refresh BEFORE it expires: when now() has reached expiresAtMs, get a new token before sending, not after a
  rejection.
- Refresh once on a 401, then retry. If the retry is rejected too, give up with a ServiceError; NEVER loop.
- Read conditionally: remember the etag per id, send it as if-none-match next time. A 304 carries no body, so
  return the cached item; when the etag has moved, the service answers 200 and the cache must take the new value.
- getItem returns the item, or null on not_found.
- Write idempotently: EVERY write sends an idempotency-key; different writes use different keys, and a retry of
  the SAME write reuses its key (a fresh key on retry silently creates duplicates).
- validation_failed rejects as ValidationError{fields}; EVERY other failure rejects as ServiceError{status, code}.

Frozen evidence (do not touch): service/, conformance/, test/integration.test.js, scripts/run-tests.mjs -- digest
checked every run. Deliverable: src/adapter.mjs (replacing the throwing stub) plus integration/manifest.json,
whose `implemented` lists the conformance case ids (C01-C10) that actually pass; most cases read the SERVICE'S
CALL LOG (headers included), so returning the right value is not enough -- the contract is about what is sent.
arguments.plan:
One card. Implement src/adapter.mjs around a shared `authorizedRequest(method, path, {headers, body})`
helper: fetch/refresh the token proactively when now() >= expiresAtMs or none held yet, attach `Authorization:
Bearer <token>`, and on a 401 response refresh once and retry the SAME request once (throwing ServiceError if
that retry also gets 401 -- never looping further); on a 5xx response, also retry once with the identical
headers/body (this is what makes a write's retry reuse its idempotency key, per the frozen case that scripts a
503 on a write). getItem keeps an id->{etag,item} cache, sends if-none-match when cached, returns the cached item
on 304, updates the cache on 200, and returns null on 404. createItem mints a fresh idempotency-key per logical
call (a simple counter is enough) and passes it through every attempt of that same call unchanged; validation_failed
becomes ValidationError{fields}, everything else unresolved becomes ServiceError{status,code}. Then set
integration/manifest.json implemented:[C01..C10], complete:true, and confirm with the real `npm test` (frozen
suite, call-log assertions) before finishing.

tasks.title: Implement the session/cache/idempotency inventory adapter and declare conformance
tasks.prompt:
Implement `src/adapter.mjs` per specification.md, exporting `createInventoryClient(service, options)`.
The service (`service/inventory-service.mjs`) is a DETERMINISTIC, in-process API whose `request()` call ALWAYS
returns `{status, body, ...}` and NEVER throws. `options.now()` is the service's clock and `options.sleep(ms)` is
the only way to wait (Date.now()/real timers cannot see or move this service's clock). Most conformance cases read
the service's call log (`calls()`, EVERY call WITH ITS HEADERS) -- returning the right value is not enough when
the contract is about what you send.

Session: fetch a token (`POST /auth/token`) on first need and reuse it -- do not re-authenticate per call. Refresh
BEFORE it expires: when `now() >= expiresAtMs`, get a new token before sending, not after a rejection. On a `401`
response, refresh ONCE and retry the SAME request once; if that retry is ALSO rejected, give up with a
`ServiceError` -- NEVER loop further.

Conditional reads: remember the `etag` returned for each id and send it as `if-none-match` on the next read of
that id. A `304` carries no body, so return the cached item as-is; when the item changed, the service answers
`200` and the cache must take the new value. `getItem(id)` returns the item, or `null` when the service says
`not_found`.

Idempotent writes: EVERY write (`createItem`) sends an `idempotency-key` header. Different logical writes use
different keys. If a write's own attempt fails and is retried (e.g. a transient 5xx), the retry must reuse the
EXACT SAME key as the failed attempt -- minting a fresh key on retry is how duplicates get created, and a frozen
case scripts exactly this to catch it. `createItem(input)` returns the created item.

Errors: `validation_failed` (422) rejects with an `Error` named `ValidationError` carrying `fields` from the
service's `error.fields`. EVERY other failure (after the one auth-refresh-retry or one 5xx-retry is exhausted)
rejects with an `Error` named `ServiceError` carrying `status` and the service's `error.code` as `code`.

Then declare which of the 10 frozen conformance cases (`conformance/cases.mjs`: C01..C10) your adapter satisfies
in `integration/manifest.json`'s `implemented` array, and set `complete: true` only once EVERY case actually
passes -- the harness RUNS every case you list, immediately.

`service/`, `conformance/`, `test/integration.test.js` and `scripts/run-tests.mjs` are FROZEN evidence with digest
checks in `test/frozen.json` -- do not touch them. Run the real `npm test` yourself before finishing; a green
baseline with an empty manifest proves nothing, so confirm the count you see names your own 10 passing cases.

Use this skill when a task touches auth, local runtime boundaries, Electron, filesystem writes, agent tools, network access, cookies, tokens, or dependency execution.

Checklist:
- Start from the trust boundary: browser UI, runtime server, local project files, NKlein SDK host, child processes, and external endpoints.
- Prefer deny-by-default controls. Any bypass needs a narrow condition, a clear error, and regression coverage.
- Treat secrets as toxic data: never log them, never persist them in transcripts, and block obvious credential writes before disk.
- For Electron, keep context isolation, sandboxing, disabled Node integration, blocked popups, same-origin navigation, and CSP-covered fallback pages intact.
- For local servers, bind to loopback by default; cookies need HttpOnly, SameSite=Strict, Path, Max-Age, and Secure when TLS is active.
- For agent writes, preserve protected-test, max-file-size, max-line-count, and secret-scan guardrails.

Example:
```ts
const secret = findPotentialSecretInText(input.newText);
if (secret) return { approved: false, reason: `Blocked write: potential ${secret.label}.` };
```

- Runtime security code usually lives in `src/security/`, `src/server/`, `src/core/agent-write-guard.ts`, and `src/nklein-agent/`.
- Desktop hardening lives under `packages/desktop/src/`.
- Update or add focused tests in `test/runtime/` and keep `CHANGELOG.md` current.
